This work is in verse form. It begins with the refutation of Dvaita. The nature of Paramātman is described through 3 chapters titled Adhyāropa, Apavāda, and Kaivalya. See Thangaswami, R. A Bibliographical Survey of Advaita Vedānta Literature. Madras: Rathnam Press, 1980: p. 334.

The manuscript in Catalogue of the Sanskrit Manuscripts in the British Museum (Cecil Bendall): p. 125–126, ms. 302, includes the commentary Kaivalyakalpadruma. Cecil Bendall notes that there is some uncertainty as to whether Ganġādhara Sarasvatī wrote the Svārājyasiddhi, but it is certain that he wrote the commentary.
It is a summary of the Vedānta doctrine in verse. See Catalogue of the Sanskrit Manuscripts in the Library of the India Office (IO). Part IV: ms. 2360.
